Definition: from G3354; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids:--firkin.
BiblicalUsage: At Cana there were six waterpots of stone containing two or three firkins apiece. The word is the measure itself, a firkin, and John names it so the reader can picture the scale of the wine Jesus was about to make.
TheologicalSignificance: I notice John counts the waterpots and their measure for a reason: six stone jars, two or three firkins each, is a great deal of water, and the miracle would need every drop of it.
